project.name: curl
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace contains a curl checkout at `f3d501dc678d80a93325bd93ab05c48855e1c0d1` and a separate `curl_fuzzer` checkout at `82eb95b410cc84579b8f9d663f2a7e38f3bdb41f`. The scored source, root cause, and sink below are anchored to the staged vulnerable source that reproduced the saved ASan crash, while `patch.diff` still matches the one-line fix applied upstream in curl.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42484290 (curl): Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE {*} found by fuzz target curl_fuzzer_ftp [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42484290
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1025` in `Curl_pp_readresp` on the staged vulnerable sources. The saved witness is a 458805-byte TLV corpus with three TLVs: a URL, an initial FTP banner, and a single `response1` blob of 458761 bytes beginning with the terminal FTP line `200 uR ff 65 0a`. The `curl_fuzzer` harness stages that third TLV as the first post-banner FTP control reply and writes it to the mock server socket. Curl reads a chunk beginning with that `200 ...\n` line, recognizes it as a complete FTP response, and saves trailing unread bytes in `pp->cache`; the later crashing copy size shows that the cached fragment replayed during cleanup is 1025 bytes long. During `curl_multi_cleanup`, `Curl_conncache_close_all_connections` swaps the still-open FTP connection onto a closure handle whose `state.buffer` is only `char buffer[READBUFFER_MIN]`, even though the pingpong reader admits cached copies up to `buffer_size + 1`. `ftp_quit` then re-enters `Curl_pp_readresp`, the cached-response size check allows 1025 bytes, and `memcpy` writes those 1025 bytes into the 1024-byte stack buffer. The patch changes the closure-handle buffer to `READBUFFER_MIN + 1`, restoring the receive-buffer extent assumed by `Curl_pp_readresp`.

evidence_note: Stage 02 used the staged `sample_info.json`, `patch.diff`, `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, `reproduction_report.json`, the saved `poc`, and the staged vulnerable workspace under `_work/src`. `trace_feedback.json` was absent and `run_flags.json` set `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so the trace is source-grounded only and no additional instrumentation or reruns were performed.

source.description: First curl-side statement that consumes the attacker-controlled FTP reply bytes and materializes them in the pingpong response buffer.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has exactly three TLVs. Its third TLV is `type=17 (TLV_TYPE_RESPONSE1)`, `length=458761`, and begins with hex `32 30 30 20 75 52 ff 65 0a` (`"200 uR ff 65\\n"`). `curl_fuzzer` stages that TLV as `responses[1]` for the primary mock FTP socket and `fuzz_send_next_response()` writes it to the socket before this curl-side read executes.

tainted_value_origin.description: The `curl_fuzzer` TLV parser materializes the exact attacker-controlled `response1` type, length, and payload pointer that later become curl's cached FTP response bytes.
tainted_value_origin.note: On the third TLV of the staged witness, these statements decode `type == 17`, `length == 458761`, and `value` pointing at bytes that begin `200 uR ff 65 0a 00 12 00 06 ...`.

root_cause.description: Cleanup rebinds the live FTP connection to a closure handle whose receive buffer is only `READBUFFER_MIN` bytes long, even though `Curl_pp_readresp` later allows cached-response copies up to `buffer_size + 1` bytes.
root_cause.note: The one-line fix in `patch.diff` changes only this stack buffer extent to `READBUFFER_MIN + 1`. In the staged vulnerable tree, every ordinary receive buffer still follows the larger contract, for example `preconnect()` allocates `malloc(data->set.buffer_size + 1)` in `curl/lib/multi.c:1539`; the closure handle is the mismatched outlier that makes the 1025-byte cached copy overflow.

sink.description: Closest project sink to the ASan crash. The cached FTP response fragment is copied into the closure-handle stack buffer without any remaining extent check against the actual 1024-byte allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1025` at this copy, with `Curl_pp_readresp` at `curl/lib/pingpong.c:310:7` as the closest project frame. ASan places the destination in `Curl_conncache_close_all_connections`'s stack object `buffer` at offsets `[32, 1056)`, so a 1025-byte copy starting at the buffer base overruns by one byte into the next stack object.

parser_admitted.description: The witness reaches curl's FTP control-state machine. The URL TLV selects the FTP handler and the staged banner TLV `response0` is the 11-byte line `220 Bbzue f2 0a`, so the `FTP_WAIT220` admission checks accept the server banner instead of aborting.

coarse_trace.summary: The `curl_fuzzer` harness parses the third TLV as `response1`, stores it in the primary socket-manager response table, and writes that 458761-byte blob to the mock FTP control socket as the first post-banner reply.

Curl reads attacker-controlled bytes beginning `200 ...\n`, recognizes the leading line as a complete FTP response, and saves the unread tail in `pp->cache`; the later crash proves the cached fragment replayed during cleanup is 1025 bytes long.

During `curl_multi_cleanup`, the connection is rebound to a closure handle whose receive buffer is only `READBUFFER_MIN` bytes, and the still-valid FTP control connection enters `ftp_quit`, which reuses the pending cached response through that undersized stack buffer.

The cached-response size guard still permits `buffer_size + 1` bytes, so `memcpy` copies the 1025-byte cached fragment into the 1024-byte stack buffer and triggers the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow write.

fine_trace.note: The third TLV in the staged witness is materialized here as `type == 17 (TLV_TYPE_RESPONSE1)`, `length == 458761`, and a payload pointer to bytes that begin with the FTP line `200 uR ff 65 0a`.
The `response1` TLV is staged as slot 1 for the primary mock FTP control socket. The macro stores the TLV payload pointer and its 458761-byte length without copying them.

After the initial banner has already been sent, `response_index` is 1, so the next mock-server write pushes the staged 458761-byte `response1` blob onto the FTP control socket that curl is reading from.

Source. Curl first consumes attacker-controlled FTP reply bytes from the control socket into `data->state.buffer`. On this witness the bytes available here come from `response1` and begin with the FTP line `200 uR ff 65 0a`.
The leading 9-byte line from step 4 satisfies `LASTLINE(line)` because it starts with `200 ` and ends at the first newline, so curl accepts FTP status code 200 as a complete reply.

Because step 5 ends the FTP response before the read chunk is exhausted, `Curl_pp_readresp` preserves the unread tail in `pp->cache` for the next call. The later crashing `memcpy(..., pp->cache_size)` writes 1025 bytes, so the cached fragment carried forward from this logic is 1025 bytes long on the saved witness.

Root cause. Cleanup rebinds the live FTP connection to a closure handle whose receive buffer is only 1024 bytes long, then makes that handle the connection's active `conn->data`. Unlike ordinary curl receive buffers, which are allocated as `buffer_size + 1`, this cleanup-only stack buffer has no extra byte for the cached-response path from step 6.

The FTP control channel is still marked valid, so disconnect does not skip `QUIT`; it drives the blocking state machine, which re-enters `ftp_readresp` / `Curl_pp_readresp` on the same connection while `conn->data` now points at the closure handle from step 7 and the cached bytes from step 6 are still pending.

On the cleanup path `pp->nread_resp == 0`, so `ptr == buf`. With `pp->cache_size == 1025` from step 6 and `buffer_size == 1024` from step 7, this predicate is false because it only rejects copies larger than `buffer_size + 1`. The present check therefore preserves the helper's implicit one-byte-slack contract instead of rejecting the cached copy into the 1024-byte stack array.

Sink. The cached 1025-byte fragment is copied into `ptr == buf`, but `buf` aliases the 1024-byte stack object `buffer` from step 7. AddressSanitizer reports `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1025` here, and the extra byte spills into the next stack object in `Curl_conncache_close_all_connections`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42484290 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/curl_fuzzer_ftp` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1025` in `Curl_pp_readresp` with stack `Curl_pp_readresp -> ftp_readresp -> ftp_statemach_act`.

format.name: curl_fuzzer FTP TLV corpus
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 458805-byte witness in `poc` with SHA-256 `a3c66a235511b470b3fa1397607b3e0b8e2d973cdc386db2acc46afb14908ed2`. It contains exactly three TLVs in order: `type=1` URL with length 15 and payload bytes `66 74 70 3a 2f fd 25 2f 2a 00 b0 46 40 54 2b`, `type=2` banner response with length 11 and payload bytes `32 32 30 20 42 62 7a 75 65 f2 0a`, and `type=17` response1 with length 458761 whose first 9 bytes are exactly `32 30 30 20 75 52 ff 65 0a`. In the staged `curl_fuzzer` harness, that third TLV is stored as `responses[1]` for the primary mock FTP control socket and written to curl as the first post-banner reply. In the staged vulnerable curl tree, that exact witness reaches the cleanup-time FTP `QUIT` path with a cached response fragment of 1025 bytes and triggers the saved `memcpy(ptr, pp->cache, pp->cache_size)` stack-buffer-overflow. This GT is grounded only for that exact TLV corpus witness, not for a generalized class of FTP replies or TLV layouts.
